recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Continue modeling duration/range length limits through Timing.repeat.bounds[x], not Timing.repeat.count, unless a new work-group decision changes that design.
issue_request: FHIR-6252 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core datatypes request asking for Timing.repeat.count to support decimal/range timing length use cases. The accepted modification rejected changing count, noted boundsDuration already supported decimal duration values, and added Range to Timing.repeat.bounds[x].
initial_application: FHIR-6252 was applied in SVN revision 5642, now git commit 2fbb4392eeaedcf258c8e4f38bbe77af755cb2d6, which changed source/datatypes/timing.xml from Duration | Period to Duration | Range | Period and updated the bounds short/definition text to cover a range of possible lengths.
additional_context: FHIR-6252 is the same Timing.repeat.bounds[x] change family as FHIR-5951, which first added Duration support. FHIR-8344 later referenced change request 6252 and was closed because the same bounds[x] family already handled duration. Current source/fhir.ini keeps Timing active/normative, and later FHIR-31559 chose an extension route for explicit start-date plus Duration/Range modeling rather than changing base bounds[x].
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active source preserves the approved FHIR-6252 Range semantics on Timing.repeat.bounds[x], and changing Timing.repeat.count would conflict with the accepted resolution.
